title: Generalizing GNNs with Tokenized Mixture of Experts

problem.claim: A single fixed GNN must fit clean data, generalize under distribution shifts, and remain stable against input perturbations.

gap.claim: Input-dependent routing can relax the stability-generalization tension but introduces routing fragility under distribution shifts and perturbations.

contributions.claim: The paper shows that a fixed inference rule can create a stability-generalization tradeoff.
The paper formalizes path coverage, router selection accuracy, path sensitivity, and routing amplification through two risk decompositions.
The paper proposes STEM-GNN, combining a mixture-of-experts encoder, vector-quantized token interface, and Lipschitz-regularized prediction head.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across eight node, link, and graph benchmarks, STEM-GNN maintains strong clean performance.
On representative node benchmarks, STEM-GNN improves the three-way balance under degree/homophily shifts and feature/edge perturbations.
The authors report that code and data are available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fixed GNNs must simultaneously address clean-data fit, distribution-shift generalization, and perturbation stability.
The paper identifies fixed-rule tradeoffs and routing-specific fragility, then formalizes them with two risk decompositions.
STEM-GNN combines diverse expert paths, discrete tokenization, and a Lipschitz-regularized head.
The authors report results across eight benchmarks and provide code and data.

source_observation.claim: The paper separates coverage and selection quality from path sensitivity and routing amplification.

interpretation.claim: Robustness problems may arise from distinct upstream coverage, routing, and amplification mechanisms.

application.claim: When analyzing adaptive models, evaluate path coverage, routing accuracy, component sensitivity, and amplification separately.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these decompositions transfer beyond the described GNN setting.

source_observation.claim: The method uses a discrete codebook to absorb small representation drift before downstream layers.

interpretation.claim: Intermediate discretization may reduce the effect of small upstream representation and routing variations.

application.claim: Consider discrete interfaces when downstream predictions are sensitive to small upstream fluctuations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when quantization improves performance or what information it may discard.

unknowns: The abstract does not name the eight benchmarks.
It does not provide quantitative gains, baselines, or statistical variation.
It does not detail the risk decompositions, training procedure, or regularization settings.
It does not establish independent verification or reproducibility beyond the reported code and data availability.
